research_dossier.central_question: What happens when a fragmented comet slams into Jupiter at one hundred and thirty thousand miles per hour?
research_dossier.context: In July 1994, twenty-one fragments of comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 crashed into Jupiter, creating planetary fireballs visible across the solar system.

chronology.event: Carolyn and Eugene Shoemaker discover fragmented comet orbiting Jupiter.
Fragment A strikes Jupiter's night side, producing a 3,000-kilometer fireball.
Fragment G creates an impact scar larger than Earth's entire diameter.
Hubble Space Telescope maps dark impact bruises enduring for months in Jupiter's atmosphere.

verified_claims.statement: The comet fragments struck Jupiter with speeds exceeding one hundred and thirty thousand miles per hour.
verified_claims.evidence: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory observational logs, July 1994.

verified_claims.statement: Fragment G created an atmospheric impact scar measuring twelve thousand kilometers across, larger than planet Earth.
verified_claims.evidence: Hubble Space Telescope Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2 imagery.

verified_claims.statement: The collision released energy equivalent to six million megatons of TNT, hundreds of times the world's nuclear arsenal.

uncertainties: Exact composition of the comet's core before tidal breakup.
unanswered_questions: How frequently do multi-kilometer comets impact gas giants in modern astronomical history?
research_dossier.notes_for_scriptwriter: Emphasize how this was the first direct observation of an extraterrestrial collision in solar system history.

hook_candidates.text: In 1994, an intact ship sailed alone with dinner still warm on the table.
Seventy-two seconds of signal changed how astronomers scanned the sky forever.
The radar alarm tripped at midnight, pointing toward an empty patch of ocean.
The deepest vault on Earth held fifty records, but zero visitors were allowed inside.
A three-man crew vanished from an island lighthouse without leaving a single trace.
Deep below the Mediterranean floor lies an intact temple no diver was meant to see.
Astronomers logged the exact frequency, yet forty-nine years later the source remains completely silent.
Over twenty miles of ancient stone sat buried beneath coastal sand for a millennium.

lines.text: In 1994, twenty-one cosmic missiles slammed into Jupiter and scarred the planet.
Astronomers watched in awe as comet Shoemaker-Levy nine was torn apart by Jupiter's massive gravity field.
lines.caps: ASTRONOMERS WATCHED IN *AWE | TORN APART BY *MASSIVE GRAVITY FIELD

lines.text: The string of icy fragments hurtled toward the giant planet at one hundred and thirty thousand miles per hour.
lines.caps: ICY *FRAGMENTS HURTLED | ONE HUNDRED THIRTY *THOUSAND MILES PER HOUR

lines.text: Each collision produced colossal fireballs rising thousands of miles above the ammonia cloud tops.
The largest fragment released energy equivalent to six million megatons of dynamite, creating a dark impact bruise larger than Earth.
lines.caps: SIX MILLION *MEGATONS | IMPACT BRUISE *LARGER THAN EARTH

lines.text: For months, those scorched atmospheric impact rings remained visible through backyard telescopes across our planet.
The event gave humanity its first direct warning that cosmic collisions are an active reality in our solar system.
lines.caps: FIRST DIRECT *WARNING | COSMIC COLLISIONS ARE AN *ACTIVE REALITY

lines.text: Thirty years later, space telescopes still scan deep space for incoming missiles aimed at the solar system.
lines.caps: TELESCOPES STILL *SCAN | MISSILES AIMED AT THE *SOLAR SYSTEM
